acceptance_items.description: Documented fact: MICOM is a three-step procedure: inspect configural invariance, test compositional invariance with permutation-based confidence intervals, and assess equality of composite means and variances.
acceptance_criteria: The setup identifies the two compared groups and preserves the same composite specification and settings used by both group estimations.
The calculation distinguishes the non-statistical configural inspection from the permutation-based Steps 2 and 3.

acceptance_items.description: Open live-app detail: The official method page does not freeze the live application's permutation count, seed behavior, confidence level, or tail defaults.
acceptance_criteria: Capture the current installed SmartPLS settings dialog in a versioned live-app fixture and bind each observed default to the acceptance matrix.
Until that fixture exists, no QuickPLS default may be claimed as SmartPLS-equivalent merely from the method page.

acceptance_items.description: Documented fact: Configural invariance requires the same indicators and measurement-model specification across the compared groups before statistical MICOM results are interpreted.
acceptance_criteria: Preflight rejects or explicitly reports a group comparison whose indicator assignment or measurement-mode specification differs between groups.
The result records the model and group definitions used for the invariance assessment.

acceptance_items.description: Documented fact: MICOM compares composite measurements across predefined groups and depends on group-specific composite scores.
acceptance_criteria: The recipe stores stable group labels, membership rules, inclusion counts, and exclusions for both compared groups.
Group label exchange preserves the scientific conclusion after deterministic orientation alignment.

acceptance_items.description: Documented fact: Compositional invariance is evaluated from the cross-group composite-score correlation, while Step 3 evaluates differences in composite mean values and logarithms of variances using permutation-based intervals.
acceptance_criteria: The implementation recomputes the documented score-based quantities for every permutation instead of substituting path-coefficient differences.
Orientation handling and group swapping are deterministic and recorded.

acceptance_items.description: Documented fact: SmartPLS reports permutation-based compositional-invariance results and equality results for composite means and variances; Step 1 is not a statistical result table.
acceptance_criteria: Results separate compositional invariance, equality of means, equality of variances, and the resulting partial/full invariance conclusion.
The interval decision compares the obtained difference with the permutation-based interval and does not apply an unrelated zero-only rule.

acceptance_items.description: Open live-app detail: The official MICOM page describes result tables and decisions but does not freeze a required chart inventory or chart defaults.
acceptance_criteria: Capture every current MICOM chart, axis, series, default, and empty state in a versioned live-app fixture before chart parity is marked complete.
If no analytical chart exists, record that verified absence in the matrix rather than inventing one.

acceptance_items.description: Open live-app detail: The official page does not enumerate live validation messages for empty groups, insufficient observations, failed group fits, or unusable permutation distributions.
acceptance_criteria: Add adversarial fixtures and a failure ledger for empty/overlapping groups, tiny groups, failed group estimation, constant scores, and incomplete permutations.
Each fixture must return a typed corrective diagnostic or a fully accounted result; no failed permutation may disappear.

acceptance_items.description: Documented fact: MICOM is run before PLS-SEM multigroup analysis so group differences are not confused with measurement artifacts; Step 1 is established by inspecting setup and settings.
acceptance_criteria: The workflow links MICOM to the exact model, data groups, settings, and later MGA run.
MGA setup warns when no compatible invariance result exists and explains what the user must run first.

acceptance_items.description: Documented fact: SmartPLS compares every group selected under Group A with every group selected under Group B and provides permutation MGA plus bootstrap-based comparison methods.
acceptance_criteria: The setup supports declared group sets on both sides and enumerates every resulting pair before execution.
Permutation and bootstrap MGA are distinct selectable contracts with compatible settings only.

acceptance_items.description: Open live-app detail: The official MGA page does not freeze exact resample counts, seed behavior, confidence level, test tails, or the initially selected MGA result method.
acceptance_criteria: Capture those defaults from the current installed SmartPLS dialog in a versioned live-app fixture and bind them to the matrix.
No inferred bootstrap or permutation default may enter Standard parity before that capture.

acceptance_items.description: Documented fact: MGA compares group-specific outer weights, outer loadings, path coefficients, and other eligible PLS-SEM parameter estimates for predefined groups.
acceptance_criteria: The compiler enumerates comparable parameters using stable scientific IDs rather than display labels or table positions.
Unsupported parameter families are rejected before execution rather than silently omitted.

acceptance_items.description: Documented fact: The underlying PLS results are computed separately for every selected predefined group.
acceptance_criteria: The recipe persists group definitions and exact per-group included/excluded counts.
No pooled or scaled-pooled approximation may be labeled group-specific estimation.

acceptance_items.description: Documented fact: Meaningful MGA interpretation requires measurement invariance, and bootstrap MGA builds on group-specific bootstrap results.
acceptance_criteria: Preflight links a compatible MICOM result or records an explicit unresolved invariance warning.
Every bootstrap comparison is derived from separately resampled group fits with complete replicate accounting.

acceptance_items.description: Documented fact: Bootstrap MGA reports bias-corrected interval comparison, PLS-MGA p-values, a parametric equal-variance test, and a Welch-Satterthwaite unequal-variance test; permutation MGA reports permutation differences.
acceptance_criteria: The result contains parameter differences, group estimates, uncertainty, and method-specific decisions for each compared pair.
PLS-MGA flags the documented 5% rule at p below 0.05 or above 0.95 without reinterpreting it as an ordinary two-sided p-value.
Parametric and Welch-Satterthwaite results identify their equal- versus unequal-variance assumptions.

acceptance_items.description: Open live-app detail: The official MGA page does not freeze the current chart inventory, chart defaults, or pairwise visualization behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Capture all current MGA charts and multi-pair display behavior in a versioned live-app fixture before claiming chart parity.
Verify group identity with text and symbols so charts never rely on color alone.

acceptance_items.description: Open live-app detail: The official page does not enumerate live messages for incompatible groups, absent invariance evidence, failed group fits, or incomplete bootstrap/permutation runs.
acceptance_criteria: Add an adversarial failure ledger covering empty and overlapping groups, severe imbalance, noncomparable parameter sets, failed fits, cancellation, and incomplete resamples.
Every failed fit remains counted and the result cannot silently fall back to a pooled approximation.

acceptance_items.description: Documented fact: Users select groups under Group A and Group B, run the selected MGA procedures, and interpret pairwise differences after establishing measurement invariance.
acceptance_criteria: The setup previews every pair and workload before execution.
Saved results reopen with the exact group sets, method, resampling design, and parameter identities.

acceptance_items.description: Documented fact: Consistent MGA exposes the same group-selection and significance-testing logic as standard MGA, but each group is estimated with PLSc-SEM.
acceptance_criteria: The method is selectable only when every group-specific base estimation uses a compatible PLSc contract.
Permutation, bias-corrected intervals, PLS-MGA, parametric, and Welch-Satterthwaite choices retain their method-specific settings.

acceptance_items.description: Open live-app detail: The official consistent-MGA page does not freeze exact resampling, seed, confidence, tail, or result-selection defaults.
acceptance_criteria: Capture current installed SmartPLS defaults in a versioned live-app fixture and bind them to this row.
Do not inherit standard-MGA defaults by assumption unless the capture proves them identical.

acceptance_items.description: Documented fact: Consistent MGA applies to group comparisons for models estimated with the consistent PLS-SEM algorithm.
acceptance_criteria: A standard PLS-only model cannot be relabeled as consistent MGA.
All compared constructs and parameters satisfy the PLSc model and correction requirements.

acceptance_items.description: Documented fact: The method compares predefined data groups using group-specific PLSc-SEM estimates.
acceptance_criteria: Stable group definitions and exact inclusion counts are stored with the run.
Each group receives an independent PLSc estimation on its own observations.

acceptance_items.description: Documented fact: Each group-specific comparison uses PLSc disattenuated, factor-consistent estimates, and consistent permutation supports MICOM for PLSc models.
acceptance_criteria: Correction inputs and inadmissible-correction failures are recorded per group.
The invariance prerequisite is evaluated with a method-compatible consistent permutation result.

acceptance_items.description: Documented fact: Consistent MGA provides the standard MGA comparison logic on PLSc estimates: permutation or bootstrap-based bias-corrected intervals, PLS-MGA, parametric, and Welch-Satterthwaite results.
acceptance_criteria: Every output is labeled as PLSc-derived and links to the group-specific corrected estimates.
Parameter differences and decisions cannot mix standard PLS and PLSc values.

acceptance_items.description: Open live-app detail: The official page does not freeze a distinct chart inventory or visual defaults for consistent MGA.
acceptance_criteria: Capture current consistent-MGA chart behavior in a versioned live-app fixture and record whether it differs from standard MGA.
Verify that all chart series retain PLSc method provenance.

acceptance_items.description: Open live-app detail: The official page does not enumerate errors for inadmissible PLSc corrections, incompatible group models, failed resamples, or missing consistent invariance.
acceptance_criteria: Add a failure ledger for inadmissible corrections, singular group estimates, empty groups, failed resamples, and mixed-method inputs.
No failed PLSc group may be replaced by an uncorrected PLS estimate.

acceptance_items.description: Documented fact: Consistent MGA becomes available for multigroup comparison on a PLSc-SEM model, after compatible measurement invariance has been established.
acceptance_criteria: The Calculate surface derives availability from the exact PLSc and group predicates.
Run details and exports retain the PLSc version, correction choices, groups, and resampling method.

acceptance_items.description: Documented fact: PLS-POS settings include segment count, maximum iterations, search depth, random or FIMIX initial separation, optional pre-segmentation, four R-squared objective criteria, and a target construct for target-based criteria.
acceptance_criteria: Search depth cannot exceed the analytical sample size and target selection is required only for target-based criteria.
All four documented unweighted/weighted and all-construct/target-construct criteria are independently selectable.

acceptance_items.description: Open live-app detail: The official PLS-POS page does not freeze numeric defaults for segment count, iterations, search depth, initial separation, pre-segmentation, or objective criterion.
acceptance_criteria: Capture the current installed SmartPLS defaults in a versioned live-app fixture and bind each setting to the matrix.
No value inferred from examples or prior versions may be advertised as the current default.

acceptance_items.description: Documented fact: PLS-POS uses a PLS-specific distance measure designed for path models containing reflective and formative measurement models.
acceptance_criteria: Qualification covers reflective, formative, and mixed eligible models.
The selected R-squared targets are valid endogenous constructs in every segment-specific fit.

acceptance_items.description: Documented fact: PLS-POS deterministically assigns and reassigns observations among a predefined number of segments.
acceptance_criteria: The result retains a stable source-row identity and exactly one final segment assignment per included observation.
Excluded and missing observations are accounted for before initialization.

acceptance_items.description: Documented fact: The algorithm tests candidate observation reassignments with a PLS-specific distance and continuously improves the selected objective criterion; repeated starts are advisable because local optima can occur.
acceptance_criteria: Accepted moves never worsen the stored objective beyond the method tolerance.
Repeated-start seeds, initial partitions, objective trajectories, and winning solution are preserved.

acceptance_items.description: Documented fact: The segmentation result represents homogeneous groups whose segment-specific PLS models improve the selected endogenous-construct R-squared objective relative to the overall model.
acceptance_criteria: Results include final assignments, segment sizes, selected objective value, and the group-specific PLS quantities needed to audit that objective.
Weighted criteria use relative segment sizes and are distinguishable from unweighted criteria.

acceptance_items.description: Open live-app detail: The official page does not freeze PLS-POS chart types, axes, or display defaults.
acceptance_criteria: Capture the current chart inventory and segment display behavior in a versioned live-app fixture.
Any assignment or objective chart must reproduce the canonical stored solution and identify segments without color alone.

acceptance_items.description: Open live-app detail: The documentation notes local-optimum risk and a search-depth limit but does not enumerate live behavior for empty segments, degenerate fits, stalled moves, or failed starts.
acceptance_criteria: Add a failure ledger covering invalid segment counts, search depth above n, empty/tiny segments, singular segment models, nonconvergence, failed starts, and cancellation.
Failed starts remain visible and cannot be silently retried beyond the stored repetition contract.

acceptance_items.description: Documented fact: Users choose random or prior FIMIX separation, may pre-segment, optimize the chosen criterion, and should repeat starts; PLS-POS can be used in tandem with FIMIX-PLS.
acceptance_criteria: A FIMIX initialization links to the exact compatible source run and assignments.
The user can compare repeated solutions and reopen the selected solution with unchanged membership.

acceptance_items.description: Documented fact: FIMIX-PLS settings include segment count, maximum iterations, log-likelihood change stop criterion, optional unstandardized latent scores, optional segment-specific intercepts, and repetitions that select the best log-likelihood solution.
acceptance_criteria: Every documented setting is stored in the recipe and validated before execution.
Segment-specific intercept estimation is compatible with the chosen score scale.

acceptance_items.description: Open live-app detail: The official FIMIX-PLS page identifies settings but does not freeze their current numeric or boolean defaults.
acceptance_criteria: Capture all current defaults from the installed SmartPLS dialog in a versioned live-app fixture.
No example value or legacy behavior substitutes for an observed current default.

acceptance_items.description: Documented fact: FIMIX-PLS uncovers unobserved heterogeneity in the inner structural model by estimating segment-specific path coefficients for a predetermined number of latent classes.
acceptance_criteria: Preflight identifies the eligible structural equations and parameters before mixture estimation.
Measurement and structural restrictions unsupported by the mixture contract fail explicitly.

acceptance_items.description: Documented fact: The method estimates, for each included observation, a probability of belonging to each segment.
acceptance_criteria: Membership probabilities are finite, bounded, and sum to one within tolerance for every included observation.
Source-row identities and all exclusions remain linked to membership outputs.

acceptance_items.description: Documented fact: FIMIX-PLS may unstandardize latent variable scores before segmentation and may include segment-specific regression intercepts; it repeats solutions and selects the best log likelihood to reduce local-optimum risk.
acceptance_criteria: Score transformation and intercept choices are applied before the mixture likelihood exactly as stored.
Every repetition preserves its start identity, convergence status, and final log likelihood.

acceptance_items.description: Documented fact: The documented method yields observation-level segment probabilities, segment-specific path coefficients, and the best-log-likelihood solution across repetitions.
acceptance_criteria: The canonical result includes segment sizes, probabilities, memberships, path estimates, convergence, and the winning log likelihood.
Any information criteria exposed by the live application remain an open inventory item until captured rather than being inferred from references.

acceptance_items.description: Open live-app detail: The official page does not freeze current FIMIX-PLS chart types or display defaults.
acceptance_criteria: Capture all current probability, segment, likelihood, and comparison charts in a versioned live-app fixture.
Chart data and selected solution identity must round-trip from the canonical result.

acceptance_items.description: Open live-app detail: The page documents local-optimum risk but not exact live handling of empty classes, probability collapse, singular regressions, nonconvergence, or failed repetitions.
acceptance_criteria: Add a failure ledger for empty/degenerate classes, singular segment equations, nonfinite likelihood, nonconvergence, label permutations, failed repetitions, and cancellation.
Every repetition remains counted; label-aligned equivalent solutions compare as equivalent without hiding failures.

acceptance_items.description: Documented fact: FIMIX-PLS repeats finite-mixture estimation, selects the solution with the best log likelihood, and may be combined with PLS-POS in a tandem segmentation workflow.
acceptance_criteria: Users can inspect every repeated solution and the deterministic winner rule.
A downstream PLS-POS run links to the exact FIMIX solution used for initialization.

acceptance_items.description: Documented fact: SmartPLS uses the two-stage moderation approach and generates the interaction from predictor and moderator scores produced under the selected standardized, unstandardized, or mean-centered PLS option.
acceptance_criteria: The recipe stores the moderated path, moderator, interaction order, and score scaling choice.
The generated interaction is not standardized again before the final regression.

acceptance_items.description: Open live-app detail: The official moderation page fixes the two-stage workflow but does not freeze every current live setup default, plot option, inference option, or multi-way authoring default.
acceptance_criteria: Capture all current moderation defaults from the installed SmartPLS UI in a versioned live-app fixture.
Keep undocumented product-indicator or other legacy approaches outside the PLS parity claim unless a current official source establishes them.

acceptance_items.description: Documented fact: SmartPLS models moderation by drawing a moderator to a structural path, supports three-way and higher interactions by moderating an existing interaction, and permits moderation combined with mediation.
acceptance_criteria: The diagram stores moderation-on-path relations as scientific objects with stable target-path IDs.
Two-way, three-way, higher supported interactions, and moderated mediation compile without substituting presentation-only edges.

acceptance_items.description: Documented fact: A moderator may be a single- or multiple-item construct; binary moderators require 0/1 dummy coding for an interpretable zero reference.
acceptance_criteria: Preflight detects binary coding and warns when the observed values are not 0 and 1.
Indicator assignments and transformations for predictor and moderator remain linked to both estimation stages.

acceptance_items.description: Documented fact: Stage 1 estimates the main-effects model without the interaction, then Stage 2 multiplies predictor and moderator construct scores and estimates that interaction alongside predictor and moderator main effects.
acceptance_criteria: SmartPLS's required moderator-to-outcome main effect is added deterministically when absent and is disclosed in the compiled plan.
Stage-1 scores, generated products, and stage-2 rows share exact observation identities and missing-data treatment.

acceptance_items.description: Documented fact: Moderation results evaluate the interaction effect and include a simple-slope plot at low, mean, and high moderator values; moderation may contribute to conditional indirect effects when combined with mediation.
acceptance_criteria: The result identifies the focal path, moderator, interaction coefficient, scaling, and conditional slopes.
Moderated-mediation outputs trace each conditional indirect effect to the exact constituent paths and moderator value.

acceptance_items.description: Documented fact: SmartPLS provides simple-slope plots using low minus one standard deviation, mean, and high plus one standard deviation moderator values.
acceptance_criteria: The chart stores the x values, three conditional lines, labels, scaling, and moderator reference values.
Confidence bands, if exposed by the live application, remain an open detail until separately captured and cannot be invented from this page.

acceptance_items.description: Open live-app detail: The official page explains required main effects and binary coding but does not enumerate live diagnostics for invalid target paths, missing scores, collinearity, duplicate interactions, or failed higher-way terms.
acceptance_criteria: Add a failure ledger for invalid or deleted target paths, zero-variance scores, non-0/1 binary moderators, duplicate terms, collinearity, unsupported interaction order, and failed inference.
Each failure identifies the scientific relation and corrective action; generated terms never leak as user indicators.

acceptance_items.description: Documented fact: Users add the moderator construct, draw its relationship to the focal path, and for a higher-way interaction draw an additional moderator to the existing interaction; SmartPLS adds required outcome main effects during calculation.
acceptance_criteria: The authored relation survives save/reopen and changes the compiled plan and result.
Method details explain the automatic main effect, two-stage score generation, binary-moderator caution, and simple-slope interpretation.

acceptance_items.description: Documented fact: Mediation analysis uses the structural paths in a PLS model, with algorithm and bootstrap results supplying direct, indirect, and total effects.
acceptance_criteria: The setup identifies eligible source, mediator sequence, and outcome paths from the scientific graph.
Inference settings are inherited only from the exact linked qualified bootstrap run.

acceptance_items.description: Open live-app detail: The official mediation page does not freeze live defaults for effect-table selection, classification display, bootstrap linkage, or plot behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Capture current SmartPLS mediation result defaults in a versioned live-app fixture and bind them to the matrix.
Do not present a QuickPLS classification scheme as a SmartPLS default without official or live-app evidence.

acceptance_items.description: Documented fact: SmartPLS supports single mediation, multiple parallel mediators, serial mediators, and mediation combined with moderation for conditional process analysis.
acceptance_criteria: Path enumeration finds every specific indirect route without double counting in parallel, serial, and mixed networks.
Moderated mediation retains the moderator location and conditional effect definition.

acceptance_items.description: Documented fact: Mediation results are derived from the same PLS-SEM algorithm and bootstrap model that contains the mediator paths.
acceptance_criteria: All constituent paths and effects use the same data fingerprint, analytical sample, estimand, method version, and orientation.
A mismatched or stale bootstrap run cannot be attached to mediation inference.

acceptance_items.description: Documented fact: A specific indirect effect is the product of its constituent paths; total indirect effect sums relevant specific indirect effects, and total effect equals direct plus total indirect effect.
acceptance_criteria: Hand fixtures verify simple, parallel, and serial products and sums.
Stable path IDs and deterministic route ordering make results invariant to declaration and graph-ID order.

acceptance_items.description: Documented fact: SmartPLS algorithm and bootstrap reports include direct effects, specific indirect effects, total indirect effects, and total effects for single and multiple mediation.
acceptance_criteria: The result gives each path-specific indirect effect, their total, the direct effect, total effect, and linked inference where available.
No-effect or mediation-type interpretations remain separate from the numerical decomposition and identify their decision inputs.

acceptance_items.description: Open live-app detail: The official page illustrates mediation models but does not freeze the live analytical chart inventory or display defaults.
acceptance_criteria: Capture all current mediation-specific result charts, if any, in a versioned live-app fixture.
Record a verified absence if SmartPLS provides tables only; model illustrations are not mislabeled as analytical result charts.

acceptance_items.description: Open live-app detail: The official page does not enumerate live behavior for disconnected mediators, cyclic routes, duplicate paths, failed constituent estimates, or incomplete bootstrap inference.
acceptance_criteria: Add a failure ledger for disconnected and cyclic routes, duplicate scientific paths, nonfinite constituent effects, failed bootstrap replicates, and incompatible saved runs.
An unavailable constituent effect produces a typed unavailable indirect effect rather than zero.

acceptance_items.description: Documented fact: Users model the mediator relationships, run PLS-SEM and bootstrapping, then interpret direct, specific indirect, total indirect, and total effects; parallel and serial mediators are analyzed together.
acceptance_criteria: The result navigation links effect decomposition and bootstrap inference to the same run.
Exports preserve the exact mediator routes and never flatten distinct specific indirect effects into one unlabeled total.

acceptance_items.description: Documented fact: SmartPLS models a quadratic effect on a selected structural path and computes it with the two-stage approach.
acceptance_criteria: The recipe stores the focal path and identifies the derived self-interaction as quadratic.
Only settings compatible with the documented two-stage calculation are offered as parity choices.

acceptance_items.description: Open live-app detail: The official nonlinear page does not freeze current live defaults for score scaling, inference, plotting, centering, or quadratic-term display.
acceptance_criteria: Capture every current quadratic-effect default from the installed SmartPLS UI in a versioned live-app fixture.
No moderation default is inherited by analogy unless the live capture confirms it.

acceptance_items.description: Documented fact: A quadratic effect is modeled on a structural path and can be understood as self-moderation of the predictor.
acceptance_criteria: The diagram stores a scientific quadratic-on-path relation that survives save/reopen.
Changing or deleting the focal path deterministically updates or invalidates the quadratic relation.

acceptance_items.description: Documented fact: The calculation uses latent predictor scores from the main-effects PLS model to construct the squared indicator.
acceptance_criteria: The derived squared score keeps exact row alignment and missing-data provenance.
Non-numeric, nonfinite, and zero-variance predictor-score states are diagnosed before stage 2.

acceptance_items.description: Documented fact: Stage 1 estimates the main-effects model without the quadratic term; Stage 2 squares the stored predictor scores and includes the quadratic term together with the predictor.
acceptance_criteria: A hand fixture verifies the row-wise square and the stage-2 design matrix.
The stage-1 and stage-2 methods, scaling, observations, and generated-term identity are persisted.

acceptance_items.description: Documented fact: The final model estimates the quadratic term in addition to the predictor's linear effect so the nonlinear relationship can be interpreted.
acceptance_criteria: Results report both linear and quadratic coefficients with stable path identities and compatible inference when available.
Turning points or marginal effects, if added, are labeled derived and computed from the stored coefficients and scaling.

acceptance_items.description: Open live-app detail: The official page shows a modeling illustration but does not freeze the live result-plot inventory, confidence display, or default predictor range.
acceptance_criteria: Capture all current nonlinear result plots and defaults in a versioned live-app fixture.
Any QuickPLS curve or turning-point plot must reproduce canonical coefficients and clearly identify additional behavior beyond the documented parity surface.

acceptance_items.description: Open live-app detail: The page does not enumerate live errors for an invalid focal path, zero-variance scores, overflow while squaring, collinearity, or failed stage-2 estimation.
acceptance_criteria: Add adversarial fixtures and a failure ledger for deleted paths, zero/near-zero variance, extreme scales, nonfinite squares, collinearity, nonconvergence, and failed inference.
Every invalid state returns a typed correction and never leaks NaN or a placeholder zero.

acceptance_items.description: Documented fact: Users select Quadratic effect in the modeling toolbar and click the structural path to receive the nonlinear term, then estimate it through the two-stage procedure.
acceptance_criteria: The editor provides keyboard-accessible equivalent authoring and distinguishes the quadratic scientific relation from visual annotations.
Run details and exports link both stages and the generated squared score to the authored path.

acceptance_items.description: Documented fact: Higher-order modeling requires the HCM type, construction approach, lower-order indicator structure, PLS weighting scheme, and Mode A or Mode B choices.
acceptance_criteria: Setup makes the four HCM types and each documented construction approach explicit.
Incompatible HOC/LOC direction, measurement modes, or approach combinations are blocked before estimation.

acceptance_items.description: Open live-app detail: The official HCM page does not freeze the current live defaults for type, construction approach, weighting scheme, modes, or stage-generation behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Capture current SmartPLS HCM authoring and calculation defaults in a versioned live-app fixture.
No existing QuickPLS disjoint two-stage behavior may be generalized into an official default.

acceptance_items.description: Documented fact: SmartPLS supports reflective-reflective, formative-reflective, reflective-formative, and formative-formative HCMs with repeated indicators, extended repeated indicators, embedded two-stage, and disjoint two-stage approaches.
acceptance_criteria: Qualification includes all four HCM types and all documented approaches, including multiple HOCs where the general model permits them.
HOC-to-LOC relations retain measurement meaning rather than being flattened into ordinary structural paths.

acceptance_items.description: Documented fact: An HCM is built from lower-order constructs and their indicator blocks, with specification affected by the number of indicators per LOC and their Mode A/Mode B treatment.
acceptance_criteria: Every LOC indicator binding, mode, and source transformation is persisted.
Stage-generated scores are immutable derived variables linked to their source LOCs and analytical sample.

acceptance_items.description: Documented fact: Documented HCM estimation approaches include repeated-indicator variants and embedded/disjoint two-stage workflows; the disjoint approach explicitly produces Stage 1 and Stage 2 models.
acceptance_criteria: Each approach compiler emits an auditable generated model and parameter mapping.
Stage-generated scores and repeated indicators cannot collide with user indicators or leak into unrelated constructs.

acceptance_items.description: Documented fact: HOC-to-LOC relationships are interpreted as loadings for reflective-reflective and formative-reflective HCMs, and as weights for reflective-formative and formative-formative HCMs; both LOC and HOC measurement models must be assessed.
acceptance_criteria: Result tables label each HOC-to-LOC parameter as a loading or weight according to the HCM type.
LOC and HOC assessment results, generated stages, and structural effects remain linked without duplicate counting.

acceptance_items.description: Open live-app detail: The official page illustrates two stages but does not freeze a live analytical chart inventory or diagram display defaults.
acceptance_criteria: Capture current stage diagrams, HCM result charts, and visibility defaults in a versioned live-app fixture.
Generated-stage diagrams distinguish authored objects from compiler-derived objects and remain accessible without color.

acceptance_items.description: Open live-app detail: The official page does not enumerate live diagnostics for insufficient LOCs, insufficient indicators, cyclic HOC definitions, incompatible modes, score-generation failure, or stage nonconvergence.
acceptance_criteria: Add a failure ledger for insufficient and duplicate LOCs, invalid indicator blocks, cycles, unsupported nesting, incompatible modes, failed stages, and inadmissible results.
Every failure names the HOC/LOC object and corrective action; no partial generated model is committed.

acceptance_items.description: Documented fact: Users specify an HCM type and approach, estimate any generated stages, and evaluate both lower-order measurement models and the HOC-to-LOC measurement relationships.
acceptance_criteria: The editor and parameter-table views synchronize HOC/LOC roles and generated stages.
Save/reopen and exports preserve authored HCM semantics, chosen approach, stage provenance, and loading/weight interpretation.

acceptance_items.description: Documented fact: SmartPLS applies the control-function Gaussian-copula variant to user-selected structural relationships and can include a copula term for each of multiple endogenous regressors.
acceptance_criteria: The recipe stores every selected structural path and generated GC-term identity.
Multiple eligible endogenous regressors are represented simultaneously rather than reduced to one without disclosure.

acceptance_items.description: Open live-app detail: The official Gaussian-copula page does not freeze current defaults for term selection, normality diagnostics, bootstrap settings, scaling, or extended-framework options.
acceptance_criteria: Capture every current Gaussian-copula default from the installed SmartPLS UI in a versioned live-app fixture.
Keep unobserved options open rather than inferring them from papers or older implementations.

acceptance_items.description: Documented fact: A GC term is attached to a selected relationship in the structural model; the SmartPLS control-function implementation can address multiple endogenous regressors with multiple terms.
acceptance_criteria: The diagram stores each GC attachment as a scientific derived-term relation with a stable target-path ID.
Preflight enumerates eligible selected regressors and rejects unsupported relations before execution.

acceptance_items.description: Documented fact: The Gaussian-copula approach requires non-normal endogenous regressors, which researchers must check, for example with the Cramer-von Mises test.
acceptance_criteria: The result records the distribution diagnostic, sample, missing-data treatment, and eligibility decision for every selected regressor.
Normal or indeterminate distributions return an explicit caution or typed ineligibility under the frozen method contract.

acceptance_items.description: Documented fact: The control-function approach adds a copula term to the regression equation for each selected endogenous regressor.
acceptance_criteria: A transparent reference fixture verifies copula construction, scaling, row alignment, and simultaneous inclusion for multiple regressors.
Generated GC terms retain source-regressor and target-equation provenance and cannot be edited as ordinary observed indicators.

acceptance_items.description: Documented fact: The copula-term estimate reflects the regressor-error correlation scaled by error variance, and bootstrapped standard errors test whether the endogeneity signal is statistically significant.
acceptance_criteria: Results include every selected path, GC-term estimate, uncertainty, test decision, distribution diagnostic, and corrected structural estimate.
The output avoids causal certainty language and states the non-normality requirement and method limitations.

acceptance_items.description: Open live-app detail: The official page documents model notation and result interpretation but does not freeze current result charts or display defaults.
acceptance_criteria: Capture all current GC diagnostic and result charts, if any, in a versioned live-app fixture.
Record verified table-only behavior if no analytical chart exists; the model screenshot is not a result chart.

acceptance_items.description: Open live-app detail: The page cautions that non-normality and additional limitations must be checked but does not enumerate live behavior for normal regressors, tied distributions, collinearity, multiple-term singularity, or failed bootstrap fits.
acceptance_criteria: Add a failure ledger for normal/indeterminate distributions, ties, zero variance, extreme scales, collinearity, singular multiple-term designs, failed PLS fits, and failed bootstrap replicates.
Every replicate and excluded regressor remains accounted for; no silent term removal or zero substitution is permitted.

acceptance_criteria: The authored GC relation survives save/reopen and changes the compiled plan and results.
Setup, results, Method Details, and exports link path selection, distribution checks, PLS estimation, and bootstrap inference.
